text: Princess Shruti Rajya Lakshmi Devi Shah of Nepal (Nepali: श्रुती राज्य लक्ष्मी देवी शाह) (15 October 1976 – 1 June 2001) was the daughter of King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya, and sister of King Dipendra and Prince Nirajan. She was widely admired by the public as a compassionate and approachable figure, earning the affectionate nickname 'the people's princess' in Nepal. Known for her active involvement in social and humanitarian causes, Princess Shruti participated in charitable activities focused on education, children’s welfare, and women’s empowerment. She supported initiatives to improve access to schooling for underprivileged children in rural Nepal and was involved in programs promoting skill development and self-reliance among women. Passionate about Nepalese culture, she contributed to the preservation of traditional arts and music. Her philanthropic efforts, though cut short by her untimely death, remain a significant part of her legacy. She studied at Kanti Ishwari Sishu Vidhyalaya in Tripureswar, Nepal, St. Mary's School in Kathmandu, Nepal, and later at Mayo College Girls School in Ajmer, India, completing her bachelor's degree at Padma Kanya Campus in Nepal. She was a meritorious painter. Princess Shruti married Kumar Gorakh Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana, a member of the aristocratic Rana family of Nepal, descendants of Maharaja Chandra Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana through Field Marshal Sir Kaiser Shamsher Jang Bahadur Rana; he is head of Global Banking and Commercial Banking for Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited. The couple married on 7 May 1997 in Kathmandu and had two daughters. On 5 December 2008 in Kathmandu, Kumar Gorakh Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana married Deepti Chand, a humanities student at Kathmandu's Padma Kanya Multiple Campus, who is also the niece of former royalist prime minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand. The name Shruti means "that which is heard." Princess Shruti, along with her mother, father, brother Nirajan, and six other royal relatives, was killed in the Nepalese royal massacre on 1 June 2001.
